in_sanskrit.name: राघव
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: Raghu + vam = Raghav. Raghu means 'king' and vam is the suffix meaning 'son'. So, Raghav means 'son of a king' or 'royal hero'.

in_hindi.name: राघव
in_hindi.long_meaning: Rāghava is a name of Rama, an incarnation of the Hindu god Vishnu. It is derived from the Sanskrit words rāghu, meaning 'king', and vam, meaning 'son'. So, Raghav means 'son of a king' or 'royal hero'. In Hindu mythology, Raghav is also associated with the god Rama, who is considered an ideal man, hero, and king. Thus, Raghav is a name of great significance and meaning in Hindu culture.

in_tamil.name: ரா஘வ
in_tamil.long_meaning: Rāghava is a name of Rama, an incarnation of the Hindu god Vishnu. In Tamil, Raghav is interpreted as 'hero' or 'brave warrior'. This meaning is derived from the Tamil words kuṝntāi, meaning 'hero', and kiṙampattār, meaning 'brave warrior'. Thus, Raghav is a name of great significance and meaning in Tamil culture as well.

in_telugu.name: రాఘవ
in_telugu.long_meaning: Rāghava is a name of Rama, an incarnation of the Hindu god Vishnu. In Telugu, Raghav is interpreted as 'king' or 'hero'. data.cultural_impact: The name "Raghav" holds great significance in Hindu culture, especially in the epics of Ramayana and Mahabharata. Raghav is an ancient and revered name that has been carried by several prominent characters among the Hindu community. One of the most famous Raghavs is Raghavan (Raghu), the father of Lord Rama, who is considered the epitome of righteousness and bravery. He is also mentioned as Raghavendra or 'the lord of Raghavas'. This name instills a sense of power, prosperity, and royalty, inspiring others to strive for success in their endeavors.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, the name "Raghav" carries the essence of abundance, prosperity, and divine protection. It underscores the qualities of a royal yogi, or a spiritual person who leads a rich, prosperous life filled with blessings and grace. The awareness of the responsibility that comes with wealth and power, as conveyed by the name, serves as a constant reminder for those who bear it to manage their material possessions wisely and use them for the greater good. Ultimately, the name Raghav symbolizes fulfillment, both materially and spiritually, and the honor and respect that comes with leading a meaningful life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Raghav is a Sanskrit name meaning 'touching the heart with rhythm'. It symbolizes the ability to evoke emotions and connect deeply with others through music, art, or words.

vedic_reference.note: Raghav is a name of Rama, an incarnation of the Hindu god Vishnu. In Hindu mythology, Rama is considered an ideal man, hero, and king. Raghav is mentioned in various Hindu scriptures, including the Ramayana, Mahabharata, and Puranas.

historical_references.reference: Raghav was a descendant of King Raghu, a legendary king mentioned in various Hindu texts including the Ramayana. This dynasty is also known as the Ikshvaku dynasty.
Raghav is also a name of King Raghu II, who ruled Kalinga (modern Odisha, India) around the 2nd century AD. He was a powerful ruler and expanded his kingdom significantly during his reign.

trends: Raghav is a popular name in the Indian subcontinent, especially among Hindus. It is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Raghu' which means 'king' or 'descendant of Raghu'. The name is associated with Lord Rama, a central figure in Hindu mythology, who is also known as Raghav.

Indian names are increasingly popular among the global population, and Raghav is no exception. The name has been adopted by people of various ethnicities and religions, reflecting its universal appeal.
Raghav is also a common name among Indian diaspora communities around the world.
The name Raghav is a unisex name and is used for both males and females in various parts of India and beyond.
